pa-gov-2026-shapiro-josh.name: Josh Shapiro
pa-gov-2026-shapiro-josh.bio: 48th Governor of Pennsylvania, in office since January 2023.

positions.stance: Says he continues to "take on the powerful on behalf of the people," as he did as Attorney General.
Calls agriculture key to Pennsylvania's economic development and has prioritized investments in farmers and the industry.
Working to make the criminal justice system "more just and more fair" and to support people reentering communities.
Working to lower costs so Pennsylvanians can stay in their homes, afford rent, and keep more of their money.
Aims to make Pennsylvania a national leader in innovation, job creation, and economic development.

az-gov-2026-hobbs-katie.name: Katie Hobbs
az-gov-2026-hobbs-katie.bio: Governor of Arizona and a trained social worker.

positions.stance: Supports free early childhood education, affordable child care, and access to school counselors and social workers for every student.
Plans to empower local communities to build more affordable housing and to address homelessness.
Supports repealing the 1901 abortion law and expanding access to abortion services and family planning.
Prioritizes securing and modernizing Arizona's water supply and building a clean energy economy.
Wants more funding and state police assistance for sheriffs and local law enforcement handling migrant crossings.
"Give Tennesseans back their Government."
"Provide for public safety."
"Put Tennesseans first."
Sees corruption as Tennessee's greatest challenge over the next decade.
Wants to drop taxes in all Colorado counties, including no tax on milk, and "no more extra taxes to the people."
Wants to cut federal programs in schools and give them back to the state of Colorado.
Criticizes the taxpayer cost of Denver's sanctuary city policies and calls for putting "Americans First."
Says I-25 should have a third lane next to the express lane, or no express lane at all.
Says funds for some county programs are not being used as they should be.
Says increasing coherence in government and society through "coherence principles and technologies" benefits all areas of government.
Says a Colorado technology converting methane into hydrogen and graphene could meet state emissions goals without more EV incentives.
Says Colorado has a solution to largely solve the global air pollution problem within five years.
Says too much is invested in exploiting problems instead of preventing and solving them.
Wants a new model of government based on coherence to break "the two-party stranglehold on America."

nv-gov-2026-ford-danielle.name: Danielle Ford
nv-gov-2026-ford-danielle.bio: Member of the Nevada State Board of Education and former Clark County School District trustee.

positions.stance: Running as a "Nevada-first nonpartisan," making decisions based on Nevada's needs instead of partisan talking points.
Focuses on repairing systems families rely on, including affordability, education, health care, water, energy, and government accountability.
Says she asks hard questions, follows public money, and holds public systems accountable.
Wants guardrails on student data, surveillance, automated decision-making, algorithmic bias, and data centers' water and energy use.

id-gov-2026-pro-life-marvin.name: Pro-Life (formerly known as Marvin Richardson)
id-gov-2026-pro-life-marvin.bio: Organic farmer and self-described political and moral activist.

positions.stance: "Abortion is murder."
"There are only males and females."
"Socialism is collective theft."
Would restrict campaign spending and outlaw paid lobbying so corporations and big money do not control government.
Wants to meet needs like food, housing, health care, and child care through regulating employers and landlords and fair taxation.
Would reduce spending on prisons and invest in housing, social support, and mental health and addictions care.
Calls for urgent cuts in greenhouse gas emissions and a shift toward plant-based organic agriculture and local food systems.
Supports energy-efficient transportation and increasing the energy efficiency of all buildings in Vermont.

H2CA06259.name: Jared Huffman
H2CA06259.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 2nd District and Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Committee.

positions.stance: Wants agriculture to prioritize healthy, local, organic, affordable food over the needs of the largest agribusinesses.
Calls addressing climate change "the greatest imperative of our time," requiring investment in infrastructure, new technologies, and jobs.
Working to secure resources to prevent and recover from disasters, including increasing wildfire resiliency.
Supports budget investments in infrastructure, research, clean energy, and education, plus a higher minimum wage and paid family leave.
Supports proper funding for programs like Head Start and opposes redirecting public school funds to private and charter schools.

H4CA12055.name: Ro Khanna
H4CA12055.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 17th District and member of the House Armed Services Committee.

positions.stance: Supports advanced American manufacturing and nationwide investment in high-tech apprenticeships and worker training.
Supports free public college, community college, and vocational school, and forgiving student debt for working and middle-class people.
Supports a renewable energy "moonshot," repealing fossil fuel subsidies, and banning fracking on public lands.
Says no one should face discrimination based on sexual orientation or gender identity, and supports strong voting rights protections.
Favors diplomatic solutions over military action and opposes broad authorizations of military force.
